EpiModel

Mathematical modeling of infectious disease dynamics in R.

EpiModel simulates epidemics with three classes of models, from deterministic compartmental models to stochastic network models in which partnerships form, persist, and dissolve according to rules estimated with temporal exponential-family random graph models (TERGMs) from the Statnet suite of R packages. Built-in SI, SIR, and SIS models run out of the box, and an extension API supports custom disease states, demography, and interventions for new research questions.

Model class Simulate with Contact structure
Deterministic compartmental models dcm() Population-level ODEs with random mixing
Stochastic individual contact models icm() Individuals with random mixing
Stochastic network models netest(), netdx(), netsim() Dynamic partnerships estimated from network data

All three share one interface: set inputs with param.*(), init.*(), and control.*(), then simulate.

EpiModel is the core package of a broader platform for infectious disease modeling. Visit epimodel.org for the extension packages, the learning pathway, and the team.

Installation

The current release version can be found on CRAN and installed with:

install.packages("EpiModel", dependencies = TRUE)

To install the development version, use the remotes package:

if (!require("remotes")) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("EpiModel/EpiModel")

Example

A network model in three steps: estimate a dynamic network from target statistics, check that simulations from it reproduce those targets, then simulate an epidemic over it. This runs in under a minute on a laptop.

library(EpiModel)

# 1. Estimate: 500 people, 175 partnerships, 110 with 2+ partners, none with 4+
nw <- network_initialize(n = 500)
est <- netest(nw,
  formation = ~edges + concurrent + degrange(from = 4),
  target.stats = c(175, 110, 0),
  coef.diss = dissolution_coefs(~offset(edges), duration = 50)  # mean duration
)

# 2. Diagnose: simulated networks should match the targets
dx <- netdx(est, nsims = 5, nsteps = 500)
plot(dx)

# 3. Simulate an SIS epidemic over the dynamic network
param <- param.net(inf.prob = 0.4, act.rate = 2, rec.rate = 0.05)
init <- init.net(i.num = 10)
control <- control.net(type = "SIS", nsims = 5, nsteps = 500)
sim <- netsim(est, param, init, control)
plot(sim)

The Intro to EpiModel vignette walks through each step and the analysis of the output.

The main methods paper in the Journal of Statistical Software describes the modeling framework and software design: doi:10.18637/jss.v084.i08. The learning pathway on epimodel.org orders these resources from beginning to advanced.

Getting Help

Users are encouraged to use GitHub Issues to ask questions (both technical coding questions and conceptual modeling questions), report bugs, and request new features.

Citation

If using EpiModel for teaching or research, please include a citation to our main methods paper:

Jenness SM, Goodreau SM and Morris M. EpiModel: An R Package for Mathematical Modeling of Infectious Disease over Networks. Journal of Statistical Software. 2018; 84(8): 1-47. doi: 10.18637/jss.v084.i08

Please also send us an email if you have used EpiModel in your work so we can add it to our records. EpiModel and its extension packages have been used in 130+ published studies; see the full list.
